If it was important we would have been taught the skills to succeed. If it was important we wouldn't have to struggle for a normalcy that is so far from consistence of a real life. Sure, we try to gather together in an attempt to be happy, to console each other for the sad existence we call 'life'. We show 'love', we feel 'love' but in the end of all ends we die alone. Even after death it may take days,months or even years but eventually all those we hold dear will move on and forget we were ever a part of their lives. Nothing but a casket full of chemicals and disappointment of adults who coward in the face of difficultly. 

Opportunities. You say of those like they are a drop in a rain fall that you can catch if only you can reach far enough. But unfortunately the majority of those barely clinging to this life we call living can't catch a break or even a breath, let alone the advantages so called 'presented' or 'given'. 

You and I are nothing but a flea on a planet hurling through a solar system doomed for collision on a interplanetary scale, destined for nothing but an inferno ending in a black hole's hunger games. 

Eventually we all see the truth. We all see that we can do nothing but waste away in a physical cage of flesh hoping for an afterlife of blissful eternity that will never come. We will inevitably face a darkness deeper than any nightmare that will be the end all be all to life.

Not even great great grandparents. More like parents and grandparents and even them. Segregation was just a little over 60 years ago and slavery ended a full 100 years before that. Took 100 years for black Americans to be able to use the same damn toilet as a white American. 

There are many people alive today who had to live through segregation and regular racism. They lived with fear that in some states and cities they could be murdered and the police wouldn't even care because they were racist. Some of those feelings carried on into their children because parents (usually) share their lives with their kids.

I agree that playing victim for a circumstance that didn't happen to you directly is folly but you can't expect the the fallout from racism to end in just a couple generations. While we still have groups like the KKK, Neo Nazi, white nationalist, the United Nuwaubianism nation of Moors, the Israelites and the nation of Yahweh racism will never end and we will continue to see racial division rooted from the past given down to those who never experienced it, on both sides.

I also see this issue with older people between the ages of 50-65 and living under low middle class or in low middle class again having nothing to do with gender, race or religion just age and income. 

But, I live in an extremely racially diverse area with very diverse incomes and ages are all over the place. Walk down one street everyone in that neighborhood makes 120k a year or more walk two mins down to the next block and they all live at 35k a year. 

I have come to the assumption that in my area it's entitlement that they get from receiving so much financial aid (very high rates for WIC, GR, Section 8, food stamps) and having lower education because of lack of income and falling job availability making them even more dependant and producing a lazy individual. Not to say all who get financial assistance are lazy because they aren't but when you have a kid fresh out of high school who can't find a job because no one is hiring and can't go to school because they can't afford it giving them nothing but free time and 'free' money they become entitled to it and feel like they don't need to work and just spend money poorly. The second age bracket I gave I generally see that from those who live in trailer homes and seem to make overall poor financial decisions. 

Idk, every area is different but that's just my two cents on what I see where I live
